# Growth Plan — "AI Automation for Small Business" series

*Generated by `youtube-script-writer` · applies `optimization-playbook.md` to this series.*
Goal: maximize **subscribers, viewers, and followers**. Ordered by leverage.

## The single best optimization (do this first)
**Package Ep 1 and Ep 15 like they're your whole channel, and chain the series into a binge
loop.** Packaging (title + thumbnail) decides CTR, which decides whether the algorithm even
tries the video; the series playlist + end-screen chaining converts one view into a *session*,
which lifts every video. That combination — great packaging on the two flagships + a tight binge
loop — is the highest-leverage move for a new series. Everything below compounds it.

## The stack (in order)
1. **Packaging / CTR.** Make 3 title+thumbnail options for Ep 1 and Ep 15; run YouTube Test &
   Compare on thumbnails. Target CTR **4–6%+**. Re-thumbnail any episode with good retention but
   low CTR.
2. **Retention.** First 30s is decisive — the scripts already open with payoff + a GEO answer
   block. After publishing, check intro retention and the biggest drop-off; rewrite those beats
   in the next script. Target avg %-viewed **≥35%** (these are 8–10 min videos).
3. **Binge / session time.** Publish as one playlist in episode order; end-screen each into the
   next (blueprint already sets `Watch next →`). Front-loaded Eps 1–3 (highest demand) pull
   viewers into the deeper catalog. This is the series' superpower — lift is channel-wide.
4. **Shorts → long-form funnel.** Cut 2–3 Shorts per episode from the best moments (Ep 1: the
   "5 tasks" list, the 77% stat, the reporting sleeper). Shorts grow *followers* fast; pin a
   comment + end card routing to the long video/playlist.
5. **Subscriber conversion.** Subs come from a value spike + a specific reason — the scripts put
   the subscribe ask right after a payoff and point to the *next episode*, not a generic "smash
   subscribe." Watch "subscribers from this video" per episode.
6. **GEO distribution (the visitors/followers flywheel most creators skip).** Repurpose each
   transcript into a companion article/FAQ (first 200 words = the answer, FAQ from the research
   questions, video embedded, playlist linked). Because AI-cited sources now overlap <20% with
   top Google links, these articles can get you cited by ChatGPT/Perplexity/AI Overviews →
   readers click through → subscribers YouTube alone wouldn't reach. Each episode already owns a
   distinct question, so the articles map 1:1 to real queries.
7. **Engagement velocity.** Each script ends with one specific pinned question; reply to every
   comment in the first hour after publishing.
8. **Cadence.** Batch-produce; publish 1–2/week and never slip.

## 30-day deployment for THIS series
- **Wk 1:** Publish Ep 1 (flagship) + 3 Shorts + draft its companion article. Reply to all
  hour-1 comments; pin the question. Publish Ep 2 (owns "what to automate first" — highest
  intent after Ep 1).
- **Wk 2:** Eps 3–5. Day-7 check: re-thumbnail low-CTR/high-retention videos. Publish first
  companion articles (Ep 1, Ep 8 questions are the strongest GEO targets).
- **Wk 3:** Eps 6–9 (the application episodes get the most shares/saves — push Shorts here).
- **Wk 4:** Eps 10–15; Ep 15 capstone gets flagship packaging + a "want Series 2 (scaling to a
  team)?" subscribe+comment ask. Review which format/topic had the best retention → that's your
  Series 2 seed.

## The 5 metrics + targets
| Metric | Target | Action if below |
|---|---|---|
| CTR | 4–6%+ | Re-package (new thumbnail/title) |
| Avg % viewed | ≥35% (long) | Rewrite intro / drop-off beats |
| Browse+Suggested traffic share | Rising | Improve packaging + session loops |
| Subscribers per video | Trending up | Sharpen the subscribe-moment payoff |
| Returning viewer share | Rising | Tighten the binge loop / cadence |

## Governance
This is a plan and a set of scripts. **Publishing, scheduling, or uploading anything to YouTube
requires your explicit approval** — the studio produces; you hit publish.
